title: England by decade, 1250–1500: population, land rents, day wages of farm and building workers, cost of living and real wages
source: Gregory Clark, data on the history of the English economy (University of California, Davis): workbooks 'Wages 2014.xlsx' (Nominal and Real Wages, England, 1209-1869) and 'England NNI - Clark - 2015.xlsx' (National Income, Prices, Wages, Land Rents, Population, England, 1209-1869), sheet 'Decadal' of each
series: Wages 2014.xlsx, Decadal: 'Farm Laborers, d/day' (farm_wage_d), 'Building Laborers, d/day' (blab_wage_d), 'Building Craftsmen, d/day' (bcraft_wage_d), 'Cost of Living (1860s=100)' (col_1860s_100), 'Real Farm Wage (1860s=100)' (real_farm_1860s_100), 'Real Building Laborer Wage (1860s=100)' (real_blab_1860s_100), 'Real Building Craftsman Wage (1860s=100)' (real_bcraft_1860s_100). England NNI - Clark - 2015.xlsx, Decadal: 'Pop England' (m., pop_england_m), 'Land rents' (£ m, nominal, land_rents_gbp_m). Column decade = first year of the decade
license: No licence is stated on the data page; the author publishes the series there for research use, with the documentation paper named beside each series. A subset (26 decades, 9 columns, rounded to 4 decimals) is stored here for teaching, with attribution.
notes: Workbooks downloaded from https://faculty.econ.ucdavis.edu/faculty/gclark/English%20Data/ on 2026-10-13: 'Wages 2014.xlsx' SHA-256 8959af72be11af1d574ebf69c9c31784bf385dd7a925f22aaa323e7d72a37781; 'England NNI - Clark - 2015.xlsx' SHA-256 214ae3b58c2da845b408cb18587ba1f02304a65c4fc609b0b2f6f9aa4320b090. The fetch script checks every column heading before reading. Wages are pence (d) per day; real wages are the nominal wage divided by Clark's cost-of-living index, both with the 1860s = 100. Building wages begin in the 1260s (blank before). Clark's population of England is lower than the Broadberry et al. (2015) series in boe_millennium_pop_england (1340s 4.48 m against 4.56 m in 1340 and 4.81 m in 1348; 1400s 2.64 m against 2.08 m in 1400); the chapter uses Clark's series wherever it is set against Clark's wages, so that both come from one consistent set of estimates, and says which series each number comes from. Land rents are nominal; the chapter deflates them by the cost-of-living index (rents / CoL × 100) and labels the result as an index, not as pounds.
citation: Clark, Gregory (2010), 'The Macroeconomic Aggregates for England, 1209–2008', Research in Economic History 27: 51–140, doi:10.1108/S0363-3268(2010)0000027004 (documentation of both workbooks, as named on the data page)
